TcRuntimeType.description: Ptn0SearchPartition is a runtime business object representing the Search Definition to be used during Partition searches.This object is created on the fly to contain the runtime representation of the search definition, when the createPartitionExpressions SOA operation is invoked. It is also created when user attempts to replay a recipe containing Partition Search criteria. It is consumed by the underlying search framework to execute different search filters. It is designed for internal use in the 4G search framework and should not be modified or extended by external customers.

TcProperty.description: Reference to the Search Criteria to find the Partition instances.
Reference to the Search Criteria to find the Partition Item revisions whose instances are included. This will be used if we are searching for formal Partitions.
This is set to TRUE if child Partitions are to be expanded and included when searching members. This cannot be NULL.

TcRuntimeType.description: Ptn0SearchUnassigned is a runtime business object representing the Search Definition to be used while searching for Model Elements from Application Model business Object that are not assigned to a Partition.This object is created on the fly to contain the runtime representation of the search definition to be used for finding the unassigned Model Elements.It is consumed by the underlying search framework to execute search for unassigned Model Elements.It is designed for internal use in the 4G search framework and should not be modified or extended by external customers.

TcProperty.description: This property contains the names of partition schemes defined for an Application Model, for which unassigned Model Elements need to be searched.This Property will internally calculated when we invoke get unassigned Model Elements from the Application Model.

TcStandardType.description: Ptn0ApprSrchPartition business object is used to persist the search criteria for Partition Expression in any recipe (Partition/Subset definition/Workset-Subset) The business object stores Partition search criteria and when provided in a search, the members of the qualifying Partitions are returned as a response.This business object is used by 4th Generation Design application today.Though the data model allows sub-typing of this business object, there is not much value in doing so, as this is used internally to persist the actual search criteria being used for Partition search.

Ptn0ChildParentLink business object holds the information to organize Partitions into a hierarchical tree like structures, known as Partition breakdowns.When an existing or planned ID is used as a parent node to create a new Partition, a Ptn0ChildParentLink object is automatically created. It stores a reference to the configured revision of the newly created Partition.The Ptn0ChildParentLink objects will be updated/deleted when restructuring an existing Partition breakdown by removing, re-parenting or updating Partitions in it. Though the Ptn0ChildParentLink object can be sub-classed in the dependent templates, there is no business value in it.The Ptn0ChildParentLink is used by all Partition based applications viz. 4th Generation Design, 4th Generation BOM.

Ptn0Design Partition business object is used as container in the Product Design or Partition template to organize physical data out of the box and to search design data. Ptn0Design Partition is a Static Partition. User can add new design components or can copy and paste them on the partition to add/organize in the Design partition.Ptn0Design Partition business object can always be created in context of an Application Model business object like Product Design or Partition Template. Design Partitions can be Formal Partitions or ad hoc Partitions. You can convert an ad hoc Design Partition to a formal Design Partition by associating a Design Partition Item with the ad hoc Partition. Design Partitions are configurable objects and can be configured by applying revision rules, variant rules and effectivity conditions.Out of the box Design Partitions and Manufacturing Partitions can be added as children to Design Partition. It is extensively used in the 4th Generation Design application. Based on the business needs, it should be subtyped to create specific instantiable Partition types.

Ptn0DesignItem business object is used to store the common design partition information associated with one or more design partition business objects.Ptn0DesignItem are created independently of the product design/partition/element structure and can be assigned to partitions in multiple product designs, but they can be created at the same time as one of the partitions that are associated with it.The partition item related to a partition is shown in the 'Partition Source Object' attribute. The Ptn0DesignItem business object life cycle is independent of any partitions associated with it. Ptn0DesignItem can reference design documentation like corporate standards that are applicable globally to design. It is extensively used in the 4th Generation Design application and APS platform today.
ItemRevision object for "Ptn0DesignItem" business object
Form Storage object for "Ptn0DesignItemMaster" business object
Form Storage object for "Ptn0DesignItemRevisionMaster" business object

The Ptn0Functional Partition business object is used as a container in the Product Design or Partition template to organize data functionally out of the box and to search design data. Ptn0Functional Partition is a Static Partition. User can add new design components or can copy/paste them on the partition to add/organize in the partition.The Ptn0Functional Partition business object can always be created in the context of an Application Model business object like Product Design or Partition Template in the Function Partition Scheme. Ptn0Functional Partitions can be formal Partitions or ad hoc Partitions. You can convert an ad hoc Functional Partition to a formal Functional Partition by associating a Functional Partition Item with the ad hoc Partition. Functional Partitions are configurable objects and can be configured by applying revision rules, variant rules and effectivity conditions.Out of the box Functional Partitions and System Partitions can be added as children to Functional Partition. It is extensively used in the 4th Generation Design application. Based on the business needs, it should be subtyped to create specific instantiable Partition types.

Ptn0FunctionalItem business object is used to store the common functional partition information associated with one or more functional partition business objects.Ptn0FunctionalItem is created independently of Partition and associated with Functional Partition that converts ad hoc functional partition to formal functional partition. The partition item related to a partition is shown in the 'Partition Source Object' attribute.Ptn0FunctionalItem business objects are created independently of the Product Design/Partition/Component structure and can be assigned to Partitions in multiple product designs, but they can be created at the same time as one of the partitions associated with it. Ptn0FunctionalItem business object life cycle is independent of partition associated with it. It is extensively used in the 4th Generation Design application and APS platform today.
ItemRevision object for "Ptn0FunctionalItem" business object
Form Storage object for "Ptn0FunctionalItemMaster" business object
Form Storage object for "Ptn0FunctionalItemRevisionMaster" business object

Ptn0Membership business object represents the relationship between a Partition and its contents. The content can be design content (e.g. a Design Component) or usage content (e.g. Line of usage).The Ptn0Membership object is created when a Design Component is pasted on a Partition. When a Design Component is either deleted or removed from a Partition, the corresponding Ptn0Membership object is deleted. For dynamic Partitions i.e. Partitions with associated recipe, the Ptn0Membership objects are created/deleted when their recipe is executed to identify the dynamic content under them.The Ptn0Membership object is either owned by the Partition (when the isOwningMembership business object constant for the Partition is set to true, typically dynamic Partitions) or by the Member (when the isOwningMembership business object constant for the Partition is set to false, typically static Partitions). The Ptn0Membership object can be sub-classed but would not provide any additional value.Ptn0Membership business objects are actively used within the 4th Generation Design and 4th Generation BOM applications today.

The Ptn0Mfg Partition business object is used as container in the Product Design or Partition template to organize the data physically out of the box and to search the design data. Ptn0Mfg Partition is a Static Partition. Users can add new design components or can copy/paste them on the partition to add/organize in the Manufacturing partition.Ptn0Mfg Partition business object can always be created in context of an Application Model business object like Product Design or Partition Template in Physical Partition Scheme. Ptn0Mfg Partitions can be formal Partitions or ad hoc Partitions. You can convert ad hoc Manufacturing Partition to formal Manufacturing Partition by associating a Manufacturing Partition Item with the ad hoc Partition. Manufacturing Partitions are configurable objects and can be configured by applying revision rules, variant rules and effectivity conditions.Out of the box Manufacturing Partitions and Design Partitions can be added as children to Manufacturing Partition. It is extensively used in the 4th Generation Design application. Based on the business needs, it should be subtyped to create specific instantiable Partition types.

Ptn0MfgItem business object is used to store the common manufacturing Partition information associated with one or more Design Partition business objects.Ptn0MfgItem are created independently of the product design/partition/element structure and can be assigned to partitions in multiple product designs, but they can be created at the same time as one of the Partition business objects that are associated with it.The Partition item related to a Partition is shown in the 'partition Source Object' attribute. Ptn0MfgItem business object life cycle is independent of any Partition associated with it. It is extensively used in the 4th Generation Design application and APS platform today.
ItemRevision object for "Ptn0MfgItem" business object
Form Storage object for "Ptn0MfgItemMaster" business object
Form Storage object for "Ptn0MfgItemRevisionMaster" business object

A Ptn0Partition business object is a container in the Product Design or Partition Template, which helps users organize and find data.Partitions can be used to divide a large product into smaller, more manageable sections. The product architecture typically consists of an organizational, often functional, breakdown. Partitions can be Formal Partitions or Adhoc Partitions. Formal Partitions are represented by actual Teamcenter items, while Adhoc Partitions are always created without following formal guidelines within the context of the product design.Partitions can be static or dynamic. Static Partitions are populated when end users drop or paste design components in, while dynamic Partitions are populated by a search recipe, which is a set of saved search criteria that identify the desired Partition content.Partitions can only be created within the context of an Application Model and a Partition Scheme.Partitions can be configured by applying revision rules, variant rules and effectivity conditions.The Ptn0Partition business object is an abstract business object and should be subtyped based on business need to create specific instantiable Partition types. Teamcenter exposes Functional, System, Design, Zone and Mfg Partition types out of the box.

TcStandardType.description: Ptn0PartitionItem business object is used to store the common reference information associated with one or more Partition objects.When a Partition Item Revision is associated with a Partition, the Partition becomes a Formal Partition. Partition Items are created independently of a Product Design/Partition hierarchy and thus can be assigned to Partitions across multiple Product Designs/Partition Templates. Partition Item's life cycle is independent of the Partitions it is associated with it and hence it is not affected by the changes happening to the associated Partitions.Partition Items can reference common documentation like corporate standards applicable globally to a design. E.g. in a building layout with kitchen, the basic safety standards for a stove installation is stored on a Partition Item, which is then attached to the corresponding Partition. In case there are multiple kitchens, the same Partition and thus the same Partition Item will be reused, thus allowing access to the same safety standards across the design.Ptn0PartitionItem is a generic business object. It has been sub-typed extensively in the Partition template, to create instantiable types, corresponding to OOTB Partition types. It is extensively used in the 4th Generation Design application and APS platform today.
ItemRevision object for "Ptn0PartitionItem" business object
Form Storage object for "Ptn0PartitionItemMaster" business object
Form Storage object for "Ptn0PartitionItemRevisionMaster" business object

The Ptn0PartitionLink business object represents the connection between a Partition and another Model Element (can be a Partition or Design Component or Line of Usage).The Ptn0PartitionLink is an un-instantiable abstract business object, and has been sub-typed as Ptn0ChildParentLink, Ptn0PartitionMapping and Ptn0Membership in the Partition template itself, to represent three different types of relationships between a Partition and other Model Elements.It is currently used by 4th Generation Design and 4th Generation BOM applications.

Ptn0PartitionMapping business object is used to link and navigate between Partitions across different Partition Schemes of the same Application Model.A "Mapping relationship" allows for easy linkage and navigation between related Partitions across different schemes, without actually creating a hierarchical structure. It is a 1:N relationship. The relationship has a primary owner Partition, known as the source Partition, whose reference is stored in the relation. Along with it, the ID of the target mapped Partition is stored as a loose reference (using the attributes stored at the parent class Ptn0PartitionLink).The Ptn0PartitionMapping object is automatically created when any application tries to create a Mapping relationship between two Partitions within different Partition Schemes. It will be deleted when a user decides to remove the mapping relation between a pair of Partitions. It will also be deleted when the source Partition itself is deleted.The business object Ptn0PartitionMapping can be further sub-typed in customer templates, however it would not add any functional value. The Ptn0PartitionMapping relationship is available to use for all Partition based applications. A few of the existing consumers are Active Workspace 4th Generation Design and Product Configurator.

The business object Ptn0PartitionRealization stores the configuration parameters and user options selected during a Partition Realization process.When Partitions are realized from a Partition Template to another Application Model there are multiple parameters that are specified viz. the configuration parameters like revision rule and the realization options e.g. whether to copy over the variant expressions, attribute groups from the source Partitions etc. These options along with the Source and Target Application Model references are stored in the Ptn0PartitionRealization object. This object is created during every Partition realization operation, even if it is carried out between the same Partition Template and Application Model pair.The Ptn0PartitionRealization object is used during the Update Realization operation. The configuration parameters stored in the Ptn0PartitionRealization object are used as the default parameters for the Update Realization operation. In case the user chooses not to provide any new values, they are used to drive the Update Realization operation.The Ptn0PartitionRealization object can be sub-typed in a customer template. However, it would not provide any functional value.The business object is available for use in all Partition based applications. It is currently used within the 4th Generation Design application.

Ptn0PartitionScheme business object stores the properties and common rules that govern the creation of Partition breakdown. Example properties can be the type of child partitions or the number of top-level partitions the scheme may contain. The Partition Scheme may also specify access permissions.In any Application Model, a Partition Scheme needs to be defined first, before creating any Partitions in it. Out of the box, Partition Schemes can be functional, spatial or physical. The Ptn0PartitionScheme business object is an abstract type and should be sub-typed in the customer template to support different organization schemes.

TcProperty.description: This is set to TRUE if the current session user has ADD_CONTENT permission on the Partition Scheme, FALSE otherwise. This is a Runtime property.
This is set to TRUE if the current session user has REMOVE_CONTENT permission on the Partition Scheme, FALSE otherwise. This is a Runtime property.

TcStandardType.description: Ptn0PartitionTemplateModel business object is an Application Model that represents a Partition breakdown template i.e. a stable set of Partition breakdowns that can be potentially reused in multiple Product Designs.A typical Partition Template would contain one or more Partition Schemes and a suggested Partition breakdown structure. A Partition template cannot contain any design components, worksets or subset definitions as its content.Partition templates are usually created by a configuration developer or power user. The ADD_CONTENT and REMOVE_CONTENT access rules can then be used to restrict access rights for adding, editing and deleting content in the Partition Template.The Ptn0PartitionTemplateModel business object is used by 4th Generation Design and Product Master Management - Partition integration applications today. There are variety of other applications based on the APS platform which can potentially use the Ptn0PartitionTemplateModel business object.This business object can be further subtyped in the customer templates.

Ptn0ProductArchModel business object contains the Partition breakdown (hierarchy of Partitions) realized from one or more Partition Templates.In an OEM environment, Partition Template (Ptn0PartitionTemplate) objects typically represent a product independent Partition breakdown template. The Ptn0ProductArchModel object typically is used to represent a Product specific Partition breakdown, derived from one or more organization level Partition Templates. The object simply acts as a collector of Partition Schemes and Partitions.The Ptn0ProductArchModel object is actively used by Teamcenter PMM application, for organizing the usage data under Partition hierarchy.

The Ptn0SchemeFunctional business object represents a Functional Partitioning Scheme within an Application Model like Partition Template or Product Design.The Ptn0SchemeFunctional business object is an instantiable sub-type of the Ptn0PartitionScheme business object. It provides the out of the box support to represent a view of a product based on system definitions such as hydraulics, power or electrical systems.Out of the box, the Functional Scheme supports Functional and System type of Partitions. However, this is controlled via a business constant and is configurable in the customer environment.The Ptn0SchemeFunctional can be subtyped in the customer templates however it would provide no additional business value.The Ptn0SchemeFunctional business object is heavily used in all Partition based applications e.g. 4th Generation Design, 4th Generation BOM, Program Planning, AD/ELD etc.

Ptn0SchemePhysical business object represent a Physical Partitioning Scheme within an Application Model like Partition Template or Product Design.The Ptn0SchemePhysical business object is an instantiable sub-type of the Ptn0PartitionScheme business object. It provides out of the box support to model the product content based on zones, spatial areas or other physical criteria.The Physical Partition scheme only exists within the context of an Application Model. Its lifecycle is not managed independently and is defined by the Product or Program it represents.Out of the box, Design and Manufacturing type of Partitions can be created within a Physical Partition scheme. However, this is controlled via a business constant and is configurable in the customer environment.The Ptn0SchemePhysical can be subtyped in the customer templates however it would provide no additional business value.The Ptn0SchemePhysical business object is heavily used in all Partition based applications e.g. 4th Generation Design, 4th Generation BOM, Program Planning, AD/ELD etc.

Ptn0SchemeSpatial business object represents a Spatial Partitioning Scheme within an Application Model like Partition Template or Product Design.The Ptn0SchemeSpatial business object is an instantiable sub-type of the Ptn0PartitionScheme business object. The Spatial Partition Scheme breaks down the product by Spatial location.Generally, all Partitions within the Spatial Scheme are defined by an enclosing volume that is defined by the associated search recipe. By default, all Partitions added to the Spatial scheme are dynamic Partitions and member design components are added to the partition based on the recipe.The Spatial Partition scheme only exists within the context of an Application Model. Its lifecycle is not managed independently and is defined by the Product or Program it represents.Out of the box, Zone Partitions can be created within a Spatial Partition scheme. However, this is controlled via a business constant and is configurable in the customer environment.The Ptn0SchemeSpatial can be subtyped in the customer templates however it would provide no additional business value.The Ptn0SchemeSpatial business object is heavily used in all Partition based applications e.g. 4th Generation Design, 4th Generation BOM, Program Planning, AD/ELD etc.

Ptn0SchemeSystem business object represents a logical system based Partitioning Scheme within an Application Model like Partition Template or Product Design.The Ptn0SchemeSystem business object is an instantiable sub-type of the Ptn0PartitionScheme business object. The System Partition Scheme represents a system level view of the Product. It will be consumed by the Systems Driven Product Development feature, once they adopt the 4th Generation platform.The System Partition scheme only exists within the context of an Application Model. Its lifecycle is not managed independently and is defined by the Product or Program it represents.Out of the box, System Partitions can be created within a System Partition scheme. However, this is controlled via a business constant and is configurable in the customer environment.The Ptn0SchemeSystem can be subtyped in the customer templates however it would provide no additional business value.The Ptn0SchemeSystem business object is available for use in all Partition based applications e.g. 4th Generation Design, 4th Generation BOM, Program Planning, AD/ELD etc.
Ptn0SchemeToToplineBVR relation provides ability to traverse from partition scheme to its corresponding Bomline in context of a Top Line.

Ptn0SubsetDefaults is a type of Attribute Group (Mdl0AttributeGroup) used to store target properties for model content added into a subset. It is derived from Mdl0SubsetDefaults business object.It adds Partition related properties that can be persisted as subset defaults. Ptn0SubsetDefaults may be related (via Mdl0AttachAttrGroup) to a single Mdl0SubsetDefinition. However, this default relation is not supported by any behavior currently. Any consuming application must provide their own behavior to apply the default values to the related subset content at the desired time.Ptn0SubsetDefaults is an abstract class and hence other templates and applications are expected to sub-type it for their own needs. Currently this is done in the 4th Generation Design application. They have defined the Cpd0SubsetDefaults class, to represent the default parameters for associated defaults for either aCpd0DesignSubsetElement (subset in workset) or a subset definition created within the 4GD application.

Ptn0System Partitions can be formal Partitions or ad hoc Partitions. ServiceInterface.description:
This service exposes operations related to partitions in Teamcenter. Partitions logically organize large sets of design components into a hierarchy that permits the CAD users to easily find their assigned data. Customers can represent functional divisions of the product (for example, propulsion systems or avionics), or they can represent physical divisions (for example, engine room or electronics bay). The nodes in a physical partition breakdown represent placeholders that may be populated by actual product content obtained from part releasing systems, CAD systems, or manufacturing planning systems.
Partitions can be added to other partitions, typically to build a default manufacturing process. For example, you can paste partition P1 into partition P2, where the content of partition P1 represents a set of expected components and the containing partition P2 represents a generic manufacturing process step. Pasting the generic physical partition P1 into the generic process partition P2 implies that the components will be attached to P1 with the manufacturing process represented by P2.

Partitions can be organized hierarchically into breakdowns. Partitions reference a scheme that defines constraints for the partitions in this scheme, for example, the list of partition types that you can arrange into a partition breakdown in this scheme. The nodes in a physical partition breakdown represent placeholders that may be populated by actual product content obtained from part releasing systems,CAD systems or manufacturing planning systems. These hierarchies are built using child parent links, where the child chooses the parent.

ServiceInterface.description:
Contains Search Services to search Model Content in an Application Model (Mdl0ApplicationModel) and arranging them by a specific Partition Scheme (Ptn0PartitionScheme). This Search Service provides operations that enable searching Conditional Model Elements (Mdl0ConditionalElement) in a given Mdl0ApplicationModel such as Product Design (Cpd0CollaborativeDesign) or Recipe Container such as subset (Cpd0DesignSubsetElement). The search result can be optionally exported to a Microsoft Excel file. Search service provides the ability to search for Mdl0ConditionalElement using various search recipes (spatial and none spatial). Also this Search Service provides ability to create Partition Search expressions (Ptn0SearchPartition and Ptn0SearchUnassigned).

Use Cases:
Search Service is used by the CPD application to implement Searching CPD Design Components (Cpd0DesignElement) within a Product Design. However the intent for Partition Search is not only to search for Conditional Model Elements, it is also to arrange/group the results by Partition, so that the calling application can display the results in an organized manner. The search functionality in Partition Search is exactly the same compared to the Search functionality offered by AppModel Search Service, except for this additional Group by Partition capability. Please refer to the CPD Server Functional Specifications for detailed descriptions on Application Model and Model Element Data schema.
Partition Search supports searching of Model Elements based on different Search Expressions. The Search Expressions could be

Spatial

    • Box Zone Expression (Mdl0SearchBoxZone) defines a rectangular (axis aligned) box, defined in a 3d space, which could be used to find Conditional Model Elements that are either inside/outside/intersecting the 3 dimensional box.
    • Plane Zone Expression (Mdl0SearchPlaneZone) defines a 3d plane and the search expression could define to look for Conditional Model Elements above/below/intersecting the plane.
    • Proximity Expression (Mdl0SearchProximity) used to find Conditional Model Elements that are spatially nearby a given set of other Conditional Model Elements.


Non Spatial

    • Saved Query Expression (Mdl0SearchSavedQuery) used to search Conditional Model Elements with specific attribute values. Accepts wildcards for attribute values.
    • Include Expression (Mdl0SearchSlctContent) specific set of Model Elements that are included as part of the search result.
    • Exclude Expression (Mdl0SearchGroup) specific set of Model Elements that are excluded from the search result.
    • Partition Expression (Ptn0SearchPartition) Model Elements that are members of a particular set of Partitions in the given Product Design.
    • Closure Query Expression Not Implemented in Teamcenter 9.1 Out of scope for now.



The above search expressions could be joined using AND/OR operators to form complex Search Recipes. Also the r esults of the execution of a Search Recipe could be constrained to return only a given set of object types. For e.g. the results of a Search Recipe could be restricted to return only Cpd0DesignElement objects. The callers could also use NOT operator to negate any of the non spatial expressions above and combine them in a Search Recipe (Note that NOT is a Unary operator and it accepts only one expression to negate unlike AND/OR which combines multiple expressions).
Search Service is typically used to perform the following operations:
Execute a Search Recipe: Executes a complex search recipe formed using the various search expression combinations and constrained using the search scope (Application Model, Search Types). The results of executing a search could be sorted using one or more of the attributes of the returned object type. Also the number of objects that should be returned to the caller can be controlled by setting the defaultLoadCount. If the default load count is set to zero then all the results are returned in one shot.
If the default load count is set to a non zero value, then the caller will be returned a search cursor which could be used to get search results as and when it is required. Also an active search cursor could be released by calling the stopSearch operation.
Over and above of the process of searching, the results are also grouped by Partition objects based on the given input Partition Scheme.
Sample code:
Typically following is the sequence of operations to perform a Search:
1.    Call createOrUpdateConfigurations and create a Configuration Context with a valid Revision Rule (optionally with an Effectivity Rule)
2.    Call createSearchExpressions and create the elemental search expressions
3.    Create the Search Expression Sets to join the elemental search expressions to a complex search recipe
4.    Call executeSearch with the complex Search Expression Set. executeSearch will return a default set of conditional elements (defined by the defaultLoadCount)
5.    Call fetchNextSearchResults repeatedly to get further results based on the search and each time this operation could be called with its own defaultLoadCount value.
6.    Optionally stopSearch could be called to clean up the results and this call would indicate that the caller is no longer interested in getting back the remaining search results.
Apart from execution of a search query, there are two operations that help the callers to save a Search Recipe and enquire the contents of a persisted Search Recipe. The setRecipes call saves a Search Recipe and it requires a Search Container object to persist the recipe. Currently in CPD application, this could be one of either Cpd0DesignSubsetInstance or Ptn0Partition o r Mdl0SubsetDefinition. The getRecipes call returns the search expressions and their combinations (as Search Expression Sets) of a stored recipe.
The sample in soa_client.zip, com.teamcenter.cpdsearch.PartitionSearchServiceSOASampleTest.java shows the use of Search operations for the following use case:

    • Execute a Search with a complex recipe (Saved Query combined with Box Zone and the results restricted to Cpd0DesignElement objects) and return the results organized by the functional partition scheme.

StructElement.description:
A Map that contains option name and flag value (string/Boolean).

Valid option names for _2013_05::PartitionManagement::clonePartitions operation are:
checkOutOnCreate - if true, the cloned Partitions are checked-out on create.
includeVariantExpressions - if true, the variant expressions are carried forward from source partitions to target Partitions.
includeAttributeGroups - if true, the attribute groups are carried forward from source Partitions to target Partitions.

Valid option names for createOrUpdateRealizedPartitions operation are:
includeVariantExpressions - if true, the variant expressions are carried forward from source Partitions to target Partitions.
includeAttributeGroups - if true, the attribute groups are carried forward from source Partitions to target Partitions.
includeChildPartitions - if true, the child Partitions are carried forward from source Partitions to target Partitions.
updateRealizedPartition - if true, updates the realized partitions from source Partitions.
overrideDefaultUpdateOptions - if true, overrides the default carry over options of update( carry over options that are selected during realization ) and considers the user input option values provided in this Map. Once overrideDefaultUpdateOptions is set to true, only the options with true values in this Map are updated for the Partition ignoring the default carry over options selected during realization. For example, if user has not selected carry over options during realization but want to update attribute groups and child Partitions during update, following input options values must be supplied.
includeVariantExpressions - false
includeAttributeGroups - true
includeChildPartitions - true
updateRealizedPartition - true
overrideDefaultUpdateOptions - true.

Valid option names for _2014_12::PartitionManagement::clonePartitions operation are:
checkOutOnCreate - if true, the cloned Partitions are checked-out on create. This option is ignored if the copyRealizationReferences option is selected.
includeVariantExpressions - if true, the variant expressions are carried forward from source Partitions to target Partitions.
includeAttributeGroups - if true, the attribute groups are carried forward from source Partitions to target Partitions.
excludeLocalPartitions - if true, the locally created (unrealized) Partitions would not be copied to the target Application Model.
copyRealizationReferences - if true, the realization references to the template Partitions are copied to the target Partitions.

This operation clones partition breakdowns (Ptn0Partition) from a source Application Model (Mdl0ApplicationModel) to a target Application Model. Source Application Model may be a Partition Template (Ptn0PartitionTemplateModel) or Product Design (Cpd0CollaborativeDesign). This operation can optionally carry forward variant expressions (Fnd0VariantExpression), effectivity expressions (Fnd0EffectivityExpression) and attribute groups (Mdl0AttributeGroup) from source partitions to target partitions.

Partition breakdowns from a source Application Model can be used as a template to create similar partition breakdowns in target Application Model. After cloning the user could re-orient or modify partition breakdown in the target Application Model. Cloned partitions do not maintain any references to source partitions in source Application Model.

When partition breakdowns are cloned in to an existing scheme in target model, and if there are already Partitions present in this scheme with the same Multi Field Key attributes then there will be a MFK uniqueness violation error reported for that duplicate Partitions, but this error is presented to the user only after saving of all non-duplicate Partitions.

Note: createOrUpdateRealizedPartitions operation should be used if one wants to strictly maintain the child parent hierarchy of partitions in target Application Model.

OperationTemplate.description:
This operation clones Partition breakdowns (Ptn0Partition) from a source Application Model (Mdl0ApplicationModel) to a target Application Model. Source Application Model may be a Partition Template (Ptn0PartitionTemplateModel) or Product Design (Cpd0CollaborativeDesign) or a Product Architecture Model (Ptn0ProductArchModel). The Target Application Model can also be any one of the three i.e. Partition Template, Product Design or Product Architecture Model. The operation supports full Partition breakdown cloning as well as partial (selective) breakdown cloning. This operation can optionally carry forward variant expressions (Fnd0VariantExpression), effectivity expressions (Fnd0EffectivityExpression), associated Ptn0PartitionMapping objects and attribute groups (Mdl0AttributeGroup) from source partitions to target partitions. The operation allows optional filtering out of local Partitions (Partitions which are not realized from a template Partition). When both the Source Application Model and Target Application Model are not Partition Template, the option to copy realization references (Rlz0RealizationMap) to the source template Partition is also available. Such Partitions in the target Application Model can be updated to reflect the changes from source template Partitions.

When Partition breakdowns are cloned in to an existing scheme in target model, and if there are already Partitions present in this scheme with the same Multi Field Key attributes then there will be a MFK uniqueness violation error reported for that duplicate Partitions, but this error is presented to the user only after saving of all non-duplicate Partitions.

Partition breakdowns from a source Application Model can be used as a template to create similar Partition breakdowns in target Application Model. After cloning the user could re-orient or modify Partition breakdown in the target Application Model. Cloned partitions do not maintain any references to source partitions in source Application Model. If the option to copy realization references is used, then a strict child parent hierarchy of partitions would be enforced in the target Application Model.

Note: createOrUpdateRealizedPartitions operation should be used if one wants to strictly maintain the child parent hierarchy of partitions in target Application Model while realizing from a Partition Template.

Operation.description:
This operation clones Partition breakdowns (Ptn0Partition) from a source Application Model (Mdl0ApplicationModel) to a target Application Model. Source Application Model may be a Partition Template (Ptn0PartitionTemplateModel) or Product Design (Cpd0CollaborativeDesign) or a Product Architecture Model (Ptn0ProductArchModel). The Target Application Model can also be any one of the three i.e. Partition Template, Product Design or Product Architecture Model. The operation supports full Partition breakdown cloning as well as partial (selective) breakdown cloning. This operation can optionally carry forward variant expressions (Fnd0VariantExpression), effectivity expressions (Fnd0EffectivityExpression), associated Ptn0PartitionMapping objects and attribute groups (Mdl0AttributeGroup) from source partitions to target partitions. The operation allows optional filtering out of local Partitions (Partitions which are not realized from a template Partition). When both the Source Application Model and Target Application Model are not Partition Template, the option to copy realization references (Rlz0RealizationMap) to the source template Partition is also available. Such Partitions in the target Application Model can be updated to reflect the changes from source template Partitions.

When Partition breakdowns are cloned in to an existing scheme in target model, and if there are already Partitions present in this scheme with the same Multi Field Key attributes then there will be a MFK uniqueness violation error reported for that duplicate Partitions, but this error is presented to the user only after saving of all non-duplicate Partitions.

Partition breakdowns from a source Application Model can be used as a template to create similar Partition breakdowns in target Application Model. After cloning the user could re-orient or modify Partition breakdown in the target Application Model. Cloned partitions do not maintain any references to source partitions in source Application Model. If the option to copy realization references is used, then a strict child parent hierarchy of partitions would be enforced in the target Application Model.

Note: createOrUpdateRealizedPartitions operation should be used if one wants to strictly maintain the child parent hierarchy of partitions in target Application Model while realizing from a Partition Template.
Operation.exceptionCondition:
Following are possible errors returned in ServiceData while performing this operation.
    • 280011: A Partition of given Scheme type already exists with the given ID in the current model. This could occur when trying to create a duplicate Partition in the same Partition Scheme.
    • 280006: A Partition of given type cannot be created within a Scheme of given type. This could occur when trying to create an un-allowed Partition type under a Partition scheme.
    • 97019: The "Copy Realization References" option is not allowed for a Partition Template.
    • 97020: The "Copy Realization References" option can be performed only from a realized Application Model object.
    • 97024: The Partitions cannot be cloned into the target model, because one or more duplicate Partitions are found.
    • 97028: The "Exclude Local Partitions" option is not allowed for a Partition Template.

Operation.useCase:
Users use the Partition breakdowns from an Application Model to create similar Partition Schemes (Ptn0PartitionScheme) and Partition breakdowns in other Application Models. This can be achieved by cloning Partitions from selected Partition schemes of different Application Models or cloning the entire partition breakdown of the given source Application Model.

Partition Template
(Functional Scheme)
    |....Partition1
        |....Partition1_1
        |....Partition1_2
        |....Partition1_3
    |....Partition2
        |....Partition2_1
        |....Partition2_2
    |....Partition3
        |....Partition3_1

Use case 1: Full Clone: User wants to clone the entire Partition breakdown into target Application Model.
Full cloning from the source Partition Template would result in creation of a Functional Partition Scheme and identical Partition breakdown in the target Application model.

Use case 2: Partial Clone: User wants to clone only selected Partitions from the Partition breakdown in the source Application Model into target Application Model.
User will select the Partitions to copy e.g. Partition1_1, Partition1_2 and Partition2_2 and paste them onto the target Application Model. As the parent hierarchy is maintained, the parent Partitions for the selected Partitions i.e. Partition1 and Partition2 will also be copied into the target Application Model.

Product Architecture Model
(Functional Scheme)
    |....Partition1
        |....Partition1_1 (Source Partition: Partition1_1)
        |....Partition1_2 (Source Partition: Partition1_2)
        |....Partition1_local (Source Partition: None)
Use case 3: Full Clone excluding local Partitions: User wants to clone only realized Partitions from the Partition breakdown in the source Application Model into the target Application Model.
Full cloning from the source Application Model with the "exclude local Partitions" option would result in copying of the Partition1, Partition1_1 and Partition1_2 to the target Application Model.

Note: This option is applicable only when the source Application Model is either a Product Design or a Product Architecture Model.

In all above operations, the user can optionally carry over the variant expressions, effectivity expressions, associated Partition mappings and attribute groups optionally from source Application Model to target Application Model. They can be modified after cloning, if the realization references are not copied along with them.

Variant Expressions are carried forward only when dictionary of options and values required for the Variant Expression are available for the target Partition otherwise an error message will be thrown.

Operation.description:
This operation fetches configured Ptn0Partition objects across the specified types of partition breakdowns (Ptn0ProductArchModel and Cpd0CollaborativeDesign) that have been realized from a given input set of Ptn0Partition objects in a Partition Template (Ptn0PartitionTemplateModel). The types of partition breakdowns to select is specified as an input to this operation.
The Inactive Ptn0Partition objects in the partition breakdown may additionally be filtered out.
Operation.name: getRealizedPartitions
Operation.returnDescription:
Returns the GetRealizedPartitionsResponse object that contains the mapping of Ptn0Partition objects of Partition Template and associated Ptn0Partition objects in realized Mdl0ApplicationModel matching the filter criteria that was passed in input.
Following are possible errors returned in ServiceData as Partial Errors while performing this operation.
    • 280001: Partition interal error occurred. This error is returned if the internal processing gets an unexpected error
Operation.useCase:
Users use the Ptn0Partition objects from a generic Partition Template hierarchy (e.g. vehicle architecture) to locate their corresponding realized Ptn0Partition objects in the derived (product specific) Partition Breakdown hierarchy. The template Ptn0Partition objects are identified based on the PartitionIdentifier input object.

Use case 1: A template Partition is realized into the Partition breakdowns under two Application Models. Both the Application Models are Ptn0ProductArchModel objects. The allowedAppModelTypesList contains Ptn0ProductArchModel.
In this case, a map containing a single row of the template Partition reference and the two realized Partition references will be returned.

Use case 2: Two different revisions of the template Partition are realized into the Partition breakdowns under two Application Models. Both the Application Models are Ptn0ProductArchModel objects. The allowedAppModelTypesList contains Ptn0ProductArchModel.
In this case, a map containing two rows will be returned. Each row would contain one revision of the template Partition reference and the corresponding realized Partition reference.

Use case 3: A template Partition is realized into the Partition breakdowns under two Application Models. One of the Application Models is Ptn0ProductArchModel object and the other is Cpd0CollaborativeDesign object. The allowedAppModelTypesList contains Ptn0ProductArchModel.
In this case, a map containing a single row of the template Partition reference and the realized Partition reference in the Partition Breakdown under Ptn0ProductArchModel will be returned.

Use case 4: A template Partition is realized into the Partition breakdowns under two Application Models. One of the realized Partition has a Release status associated with it. The other realized Partition is in Working state. Both the Application Models are Ptn0ProductArchModel objects. The allowedAppModelTypesList contains Ptn0ProductArchModel. The ConfigurationContext is provided as "Any Status; No Working".
In this case, a map containing a single row of the template Partition reference and the realized Partition reference to the Partition with Release status will be returned. The Working Partition will not be configured.

Use case 5: In the cases where either the template Partition is not realized into any Partition Breakdowns, or invalid template Partition input, no specific error will be thrown. Instead, an empty map will be returned, indicating that there are no realized Partitions available for the input provided.

ParameterInfo.description: A vector of GetRealizedPartitionsInputData objects, each containing the list of PartitionIdentier objects, ConfigurationContext object and the allowed Mdl0ApplicationModel type names.

Operation.description: This operation can be used to fetch top level partitions(Ptn0Partition) for a Partition Schemes(Ptn0PartitionScheme) within an Application Model e.g., a Product Design (Cpd0CollaborativeDesign). Operation.useCase:

Top level Partitions in a Partition scheme are the Partitions which are not children of any other Partitions. There can be more than one top level Partition for a scheme.

This operation returns all the top level partitions (Ptn0Partition) for an input Partition Scheme (Ptn0PartitionScheme) associated to the input BOMView (PSBOMView). Additional options for partition output, for example whether to include configured out partitions or not, can also be specified on the request. If include configured out partitions option is specified then both configured in and configured out partitions, based on the input configuration context (ConfigurationContext), are retrieved, and returned in the response. The default is to not include configured out partitions and return only configured in partitions.
Operation.name: getTopLevelPartitionsInBOMView2
Operation.returnDescription:
Top level Partitions along with the corresponding Partition Scheme. Optionally it can return top level partitions that are configured out for the input configuration context if desired.

The following partial errors may be returned if input Ptn0PartitionScheme object is null
•    280034 An invalid input object is supplied. Please check the Teamcenter server syslog file for more information.
Operation.useCase:
In Structure Partitions, users can create Partition Breakdowns for a partition scheme and may want to browse through this breakdown from top to bottom. In such cases, user may start with top level Partition for a scheme and then browse through its children partitions.

Users can query for all the top level Partitions for a set of Partition Schemes within the corresponding PSBOMView by specifying both the Partition Schemes and their respective PSBOMView as input parameters. Based on the input Configuration Context, top level partitions are returned in the response. Moreover, if it is desired to retrieve configured out partitions in addition to configured in partitions then it can be done by specifying the input parameter includeConfiguredOutPartitions and setting its value to True.

Use case 1:
A user creates a Partition hierarchy with Ptn0Partition objects. The system creates partition-to-partition links (Ptn0ChildParentLink). User creates memberships between leaf level partition (Ptn0Partition) and BOMLines (Teamcenter::BOMLine).
The top-level partitions can be retrieved by specifying configuration context (ConfigurationContext), PSBOMView, PartitionScheme (Ptn0PartitionScheme) and includeConfiguredOutPartitions input argument as “True”. The system will return both configured in and configured out partitions based on the input configuration context.

ParameterInfo.description: A list of GetTopLevelPtnsInBOMViewInputInfo2 objects.

Operation.description: This service operation is used to create the snapshot of the members which are attached to the input Partition dynamically. Inputs Partition and configuration context, are used to get all the existing Members of Partition. The members which are added in dynamic mode are persisted by creating static Membership objects for them.
Operation.exceptionCondition:
Following are possible errors returned in ServiceData from partitions module while performing this operation.
    • 280001        Partition internal error.
    • 280009        Access privilege error.

It may also contain error related to object delete and object creation errors.
Operation.name: persistDynamicMembers
Operation.returnDescription:
Exception occurred while performing persist dynamic member operation. The errors are returned in ServiceData. There are no plain/updated/created objects returned in ServiceData.
If user does not have the required access privileges for performing operation it will return error.
Operation.useCase:
Use Case : Persist Dynamic Members of input partition.
    • Create Collaborative design in given application model.
    • Create Partition Scheme and configuration context in above product design.
    • Create Partition and Design Components in Partition Scheme and product design

         respectively.
    • Update Partition with Members in dynamic mode by updating recipe.
    • Call persist dynamic SOA using above Partition and configuration context

         This use case will execute in following sequence, to persist the dynamic members of given partition.
                    1. Use input Partition and the configuration context to get all the existing memberships for this Partition.
                    2. Delete all the memberships got from step no. 1.
                    3. Get dynamic members for input Partition.
                    4. Create static memberships in bulk for all the dynamic members (from step 3) to input Partition.

    • This will convert all the dynamic members in static ones by creating a static Membership for all members updated in dynamic mode.


All the dynamic Members of input Partition are now static after creating membership objects in database.

ParameterInfo.description: Partition whose dynamic members need to be persisted as static memberships with isFromRecipe set to TRUE.

Operation.description:
This operation updates the given input Partition with the supplied input Partitions list. Partitions can be added as children or parents for a given input Partition.

Operation.description:
This operation updates the given input Partition with the Members supplied in a members list. Members can be added/removed/replaced for a given Partition.
User performing this operation needs privileges on partition or members as ADD/REMOVE_CONTENT or WRITE respectively, depending upon ownership of Membership object. If user does not have required privileges or any of the validation fails it returns error in serviceData along with failed members and error code for each failed member in UpdateMemberRespose structure.
Operation.exceptionCondition:
Following error specific to partition are returned.
    • 280009(Error)     Access related error, user doesnot have required privileges to perform update member operation.
    • 280001(Error)     Partition interal error occurred.
    • 280002(Error)     Invalid member, member is not of the expected business object type.
Operation.name: updateMembers
Operation.returnDescription: The exception occurred during the operation are returned in <font face="courier" height="10">ServiceData</font>.It also returns failed member and corresponding error related to that failed member.
Operation.useCase:
Use Case 1: Add members to Partition

User can add members to the partition as follows.
1.    Creates the Product Design in a given application model.
2.    Creates Partition Scheme under the product design created in step1.
3.    Creates Partition under Partition Scheme created in step2.
4.    Creates Design Components directly under Partition created in step3.
5.    User can also configure the revision rule while performing this operation and this rule will be passed to the SOA.

Operation code ADD will be used for this use case, user can define the way memberships will be created in data base by selecting proper predefined value in contentPersistenceMode parameter. That is STATIC / DYNAMIC /AUTO /ALL_MODE.

Use Case 2: Replace members of the input partition list
Members of the existing Partition can be replaced with the new set of input members list as follows.
1.    User has Partition and Design Components under it as created in use case 1.
2.    Now Design Component under the Partition need to be replaced with different Design Components.
3.    User selects set of new design components and paste it under the existing partition.
4.    This operation will remove all the existing design components from the partition and replace with new design components.
5.    User can also configure the revision rule and pass it to this SOA.
Operation code REPLACE will be used for this use case, user can define the way new membership objects will be created in database using contentPersistenceMode parameter. That is user can select any of the modes from STATIC/ DYNAMIC/ AUTO/ ALL_MODE.

Use Case 3: Remove members of the input partition list
Members of the existing Partition can be removed with the set of input members list.
1.    User has created Partition with few design components under it same as use case1.
2.    Design Components are selected and deleted.
3.    This operation will remove the links between Partition and Design Components by deleting membership object or recipe.
Operation code REMOVE will be used in this use case.

ParameterInfo.description:
Vector of UpdateMembersInputInfo containing following details to carry out operation
    • inputPartition
    • membersList
    • opCode
    • contentPersistenceMode
    • configurationContext

Operation.description:
Operation that executes a search based on an input Search Recipe and returns the list of Model Elements (Mdl0ModelElement) back to the caller. Search Recipe could be a complex expression set that combines multiple simpler search terms (both spatial and non spatial) in a logical sequence.
Search is always executed within the scope of an Application Model and all the Model Elements returned belong to the given Application Model. executeSearch operation uses the configuration information given in the recipe to configure the results of a search (Both Revision and Effectivity Configurations).
The results of a search are returned one set at a time based on the defaultLoadCount specified in the SearchOptions. The SearchResponse also contains a Search Cursor object that the caller could use to fetch the next set of results by invoking the fetchNextSearchResults call. Search options also gives the caller the ability to sort the results of a search using any (one or more) of the attributes proeprties of the returned objects.
The PartitionScope specifies the grouping by which the search results should be grouped or organized. It contains a partition scheme (Ptn0PartitionScheme) name and a flag that specifies whether the immediate partitions are the only ones that need to be considered. The SearchResponse contains the results grouped based on Partitions in which the search results have membership, in the given partition scheme.

The results of the execute search operation could be constrained by the search scope which is part of the search recipe and organized by the search options. Also the results of a search are organized by Partitions based on the input Partition Scheme.

Operation.description:
This operation stops further loading of objects from a previously executed search and clears all the memory allocated for the search operation. It deletes the search cursor and the list of Model Elements that are kept track by the Search cursor from the Server Memory.
The stopSearch does not unload any previously loaded Model Elements. Also there is no locking or unlocking performed by the stopSearch operation.
Operation.name: stopSearch
Operation.returnDescription: Returns stopSearchResponse data structure
Operation.useCase: When a search is executed in CPD and the search returns a large set of objects. The server process keeps the results of a search using a search cursor object. At each <font face="courier" height="10">fetchNextSearchResults</font> operation, the results are further filtered and returned in batches specified by the load count. However if the caller is not interested in consuming the search results further, then a <font face="courier" height="10">stopSearch</font> could be called to release all the resources allocated for that search operation. This includes dropping the runtime search cursor object and the list of Model Elements kept track by the cursor.
